subject: Post-demo: Aerolink performance onboarding & streaming concurrency plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@aerolink.io>, Aerolink QA <qa@aerolink.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Aerolink performance onboarding & streaming concurrency plan

Hi Sanjay / QA team —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load rehearsal scheduled:

Summary from call
- SLO targets you emphasized: p95 (single-turn generation) <= 120ms; streaming per-token tail < 200ms for interactive flows.
- Target load profile: 600 rps sustained for non-streaming endpoints; up to 120 concurrent streaming sessions for the chat path (steady-state). Bursts expected up to 900 rps for 3–5 minute intervals.
- Success criteria for rehearsal: no p95 regression >20% vs baseline, error rate <0.5%, no connection drops for streaming >1%.

What we need from you to run the customer-led test
1) Test accounts: list of test user accounts / tokens you’ll use (csv is fine).
2) k6/Locust script: your current script(s) — we can run yours or provide a Redwood-provided starter.
3) IP allowlist: the network ranges to add on your side for our test runners (if you prefer, we can run entirely from your infra).
4) Preferred test window(s) in UTC. We recommend a 2-hour window with a 30-minute ramp (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) for safety.

I’ve attached a short SLO template (redwood_slo_template.xlsx) you can use to confirm pass/fail thresholds and the type of metrics we’ll collect. If you want us to run the test from Redwood, we’ll provide a pre-built k6 streaming script and dedicated test accounts. If you plan to run from your environment, please share the script so Rishi can review for headers and keepalive behavior.

Proposed immediate next steps
- Sanjay: share test_accounts.csv and the k6/Locust script you plan to run.
- Aerolink QA: confirm 2 candidate windows (UTC) in the next 7 days.
- Rishi (cc): we’ll need the allowlist CIDRs to get traffic routing in place.

Thanks — aiming to lock the window by end of day tomorrow so we can prep.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Date: 2028-03-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Aerolink performance onboarding & streaming concurrency plan

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. We’re aligned and can run a rehearsal next week. Quick responses inline: 

1) Test accounts: attaching test_accounts.csv (service/test users + bearer tokens).
2) k6 script: attaching our starter k6 script (aerolink_k6_stream_v1.js). We wrote the streaming logic against your streaming endpoint; it opens long-lived WS connections and emits messages at configured inter-token intervals.
3) IP allowlist: we’ll need the specific CIDRs you’ll run from (or indicate if you’ll run from our infra).
4) Windows: proposed windows (UTC): 2028-03-16 02:00–04:00 or 2028-03-17 20:00–22:00. Prefer the 16th if that works for Redwood ops.

A couple of notes:
- The script currently ramps to target over 10 minutes. We can update it to follow your recommended ramp steps if you prefer.
- We’ll throttle token refreshes to mimic 30k daily MAU; let us know if you need different session semantics.

I’ve attached the files mentioned. Let me know the allowlist CIDRs and any headers or sampling we should add to the requests for tracing.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Engineering, Aerolink Labs
sanjay@aerolink.io

Attachments: aerolink_k6_stream_v1.js, test_accounts.csv
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2028-03-15T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Aerolink performance onboarding & streaming concurrency plan

Thanks Sanjay — attaching a short SLO checklist for reference (redwood_slo_template.xlsx) and some operational requirements from the SRE side: 

IP allowlist (egress/source ranges) we’ll use for the Redwood-run tests:
- 34.82.10.0/24
- 34.82.11.0/24
- 35.201.45.0/24

Network / test behavior notes
- Ramp pattern: 10% (10 mins) -> 25% (10 mins) -> 50% (10 mins) -> 100% (hold 30–60 mins) to spot regressions and warm caches. If Aerolink prefers a single 30-minute ramp, confirm, but we prefer staged ramp.
- Streaming: keepalive ping interval 15s, idle timeout 90s. Please ensure your LB and proxies allow long-lived connections for the duration.
- Headers: include X-Redwood-Test: aerolink-rehearsal and X-Trace-Id per request (we’ll populate).
- Observability: we will push a small stats/webhook during the run; please whitelist 34.82.12.5 for metric ingestion if needed.

If Aerolink wants to run the test from their environment using their runners, we’ll review their script for proper headers and KV cache behavior. Otherwise, Redwood will execute from the above egress ranges.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Rishi / Vanessa — thanks for the detail. We’ll add the three CIDRs to the allowlist on our side. Confirming the preferred window: 2028-03-16 02:00–04:00 UTC works for our infra team.

We’ll also update the k6 script to implement the staged ramp you suggested and include the X-Redwood-Test and X-Trace-Id headers. Expect an updated aerolink_k6_stream_v2.js in your Drive link by EOD.

One operational question: for streaming sessions we’ll simulate N=120 concurrent sessions sustained for 30 minutes; is that the agreed steady-state? We’ll follow the ramp to get there.

— Sanjay
